solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Group returning after spring floods (6)

indicators.note: going back, so the word is read backwards
places the reversed group behind SPA

blocks.note: a spa is a mineral spring
a set is a group; turned round it gives TES

annotation.surface: A band makes its comeback after the spring rains have flooded everything.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spring' reads as the season but is a water source, and 'floods' at the end looks like a verb while it is the plural noun defined.
annotation.definitionFit: Spates are sudden floods, as in a river in spate.

entries.clue: Vessels lean, capsizing in period where progress is halted (3,4)

indicators.note: turning over, so in a down entry the letters read upside down, i.e. reversed

blocks.note: to tip is to lean over

annotation.surface: Ships listing and overturning during a lull in a voyage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' and 'capsizing' paint ships at sea, but the vessels are kitchen pots. POTS TIP, turned over as a whole, becomes PIT STOP.
annotation.definitionFit: A pit stop is a brief halt, as a racing car stops in the pits.

entries.clue: Exercises embraced by seaman to become thinner (5)

indicators.note: the exercises are held inside the seaman

blocks.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

annotation.surface: A sailor puts himself through a workout programme to slim down.
annotation.walkthrough: Sailors were once called tars, probably from the tarpaulin they worked with; setters use the word constantly.
annotation.definitionFit: To taper is to become gradually thinner towards one end.

entries.clue: Aware male’s dividing opinion (9)

indicators.note: the male letter splits the other word in two

annotation.surface: A perceptive man is splitting opinion.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's in 'male's' is not a possessive but a contraction of 'male is', which makes the male the one doing the dividing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sentiment is a view one holds, as in 'I share your sentiments'.

entries.clue: Having something oily manufactured in self-contained unit (7)

indicators.note: the word for manufactured is put inside the unit

blocks.note: a pod is a detachable self-contained unit, as on a spacecraft

annotation.surface: Something greasy has been produced inside a sealed module.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Having something oily' is an odd-looking definition because the answer is an adjective: hair that has had pomade put on it.
annotation.definitionFit: Pomaded hair has had pomade, a scented oily dressing, applied to it.

entries.clue: Nameless dupe must keep quiet? Bah! (5)

indicators.note: having no name, so the dupe word loses its N, the abbreviation for name
the shortened dupe holds the quiet word inside

blocks.note: a dupe is a PAWN; drop N for name

annotation.surface: An anonymous stooge is told to hush, and someone scoffs.
annotation.walkthrough: A pawn is someone used by others, hence a dupe.
annotation.definitionFit: Pshaw and bah are both dismissive exclamations of contempt.

entries.clue: Splendid Scot has joke, one being taken in (8)

indicators.note: the joke and the one go inside the Scot

blocks.note: Mac is a stock name for a Scotsman

annotation.surface: A fine Scotsman tells a joke, and somebody falls for it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' sounds like someone fooled by the joke; here it just means put inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something majestic is stately and splendid, like a royal procession.

entries.clue: Minimal flow ending in dead river in northern England (7)

indicators.note: take the last letter of the next word

blocks.note: the Ribble flows through Lancashire to the Irish Sea

annotation.surface: A trickle is all that is left in a dried-up northern river.
annotation.walkthrough: The Ribble is a real river in Lancashire and Yorkshire; its name is the bulk of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A dribble is a feeble trickle of liquid.

entries.clue: Dirty revolutionary, over time, was domiciled (5)

indicators.note: turned round, so the word is read backwards
in a down entry, placed above the T

blocks.note: lewd = dirty, smutty; reversed to DWEL

annotation.surface: A grubby rebel lived somewhere for a while.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel, but it tells you to turn LEWD round.
annotation.definitionFit: Dwelt means lived, resided somewhere.

entries.clue: Speed up what grape-treaders do (4,2,3,5)

blocks.note: slang for press the accelerator, like 'step on the gas'
treading grapes literally means standing on their juice

annotation.surface: A question of how to hurry the old way of treading grapes for wine.
annotation.walkthrough: Juice is slang for fuel, so stepping on it means accelerating; the second half takes the phrase literally.
annotation.definitionFit: To step on the juice is to press the accelerator, going faster.

entries.clue: Plain hat worn by troublemaker (6)

indicators.note: the hat goes round the troublemaker, as a hat sits around a head

blocks.note: lid is slang for a hat

annotation.surface: A simple hat is worn by a mischief-maker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like a description of the hat but is the definition, in its sense of clear.
annotation.definitionFit: Limpid means clear, as plain or lucid writing is.

entries.clue: Footballers in Europe struggle with selection process maybe (9)

blocks.note: Inter Milan, the Italian football club

annotation.surface: A European football team battles over its player selection.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' signals that an interview is just one example of a selection process.
annotation.definitionFit: An interview is a common way of selecting candidates for a job.

entries.clue: Sailor comes in drunk — one on foot? (5)

indicators.note: the sailor enters the drunk

annotation.surface: A sailor staggers in drunk, wondering whether someone is walking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One on foot' suggests a pedestrian; it is something worn on a foot.
annotation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog, worn on the foot.

entries.clue: A youngster suffering setback in stage of biological development (4)

indicators.note: set back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a pup is a young animal

annotation.surface: A child hits a setback at some point in growing up.
annotation.walkthrough: A PUP read backwards is PUPA.
annotation.definitionFit: The pupa is the stage between larva and adult in an insect's development.

entries.clue: Grace appears to hide wrinkles? (10)

indicators.note: the first word conceals the second inside it

blocks.note: lines on a face are wrinkles

annotation.surface: A woman called Grace seems to be concealing her wrinkles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grace' at the front reads as a woman's name but is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Seemliness is decorum, propriety, a kind of grace.

entries.clue: Make vicars agitated excluding American Nonconformists (9)

indicators.note: stirred up, so the letters are rearranged
leave out the A for American

blocks.note: A = American, removed from the fodder

annotation.surface: Stirring up clergymen, but not the American ones, creates dissenters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nonconformists' sounds like the Nonconformist churches, a neat fit with the vicars, but it just means independent-minded people.
annotation.definitionFit: Mavericks are unorthodox people who refuse to conform.

entries.clue: One preserves church book with page missing (6)

definitions.note: 'One preserves' is a noun phrase: one who preserves.

indicators.note: drop the P, the abbreviation for page

blocks.note: a psalter is a book of psalms used in church

annotation.surface: Someone takes care of a church service book that is missing a leaf.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Preserves' looks like care for an old book; it means preserves food with salt.
annotation.definitionFit: A salter preserves meat or fish by salting it.

entries.clue: Italian seaport’s migratory birds gathering around mid-autumn (8)

indicators.note: the birds surround the month

blocks.note: NOV = November; astronomical autumn runs from late September to late December

annotation.surface: Birds on migration flock around an Italian port in the middle of autumn.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's makes the definition an adjective, 'belonging to the seaport', so the answer is the Italian adjective for Genoa rather than the city.
annotation.definitionFit: The Italian adjective from Genova (Genoa), familiar from pesto alla genovese.

entries.clue: Not working to hold line, causing deviation (10)

indicators.note: the first word holds the line inside it

annotation.surface: A broken device keeps the line from running straight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Line' is one of the commonest single-letter abbreviations: L.
annotation.definitionFit: Deflective describes something that turns things aside from their course.

entries.clue: Cinema left abandoned, shelter for a Greek character (7)

indicators.note: wild, unrestrained, so the letters are rearranged
the rearranged letters go round the A and the Greek letter

blocks.note: LEFT rearranged, split round the middle
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

annotation.surface: A cinema lies deserted, giving refuge to a Greek person.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person from Greece but is a letter. A fleapit is British slang for a shabby old cinema.
annotation.definitionFit: Fleapit is a jocular British term for a run-down cinema.

entries.clue: My cathedral city with saint forgotten (4)

indicators.note: the S for saint is left out

blocks.note: the Somerset city that is England's smallest cathedral city

annotation.surface: Someone talks about their home cathedral city that has lost its patron saint.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My' reads as a possessive but is the exclamation, as in 'My, my!' or 'Well, well!'. WELLS in Somerset is England's smallest cathedral city.
annotation.definitionFit: My! and Well! are both exclamations of surprise.

entries.clue: Avoiding temptress, like one against being ensnared (7)

indicators.note: the three short pieces are trapped inside the temptress

blocks.note: Eve tempted Adam with the apple

annotation.surface: Someone steers clear of a seductress, like a man set against being trapped.
annotation.walkthrough: Eve is the crossword's standard temptress, from the Garden of Eden story.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an evasive answer avoids the question.

entries.clue: Office worker in US thus assumes control of X (5)

indicators.note: takes over, taking the number into its hands

blocks.note: X is ten in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: An American clerk takes charge of a mysterious X.
annotation.walkthrough: 'X' looks like an unknown quantity or a mark, but it is the Roman numeral.
annotation.definitionFit: Steno is American shorthand for a stenographer, a shorthand typist.

entries.clue: Southern district of city, green area (5)

blocks.note: a ward is an electoral district of a city

annotation.surface: A park in the south of a city.
annotation.walkthrough: A city ward is a local government district, the unit a councillor represents.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sward is a literary word for a stretch of grassy turf, such as a village green.

entries.clue: Blood beginning to pour with a frenzy around hospital department (9)

indicators.note: take the first letter of the next word
the frenzy goes round the department

annotation.surface: Blood starts to pour as a frenzy breaks out around a hospital ward.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blood' reads as what pours, but is the definition in its sense of lineage.
annotation.definitionFit: Blood means ancestry, as in 'of royal blood'.

entries.clue: Foolish requirement for infant’s bedroom? (5)

annotation.surface: A silly thing to need in a baby's nursery.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'bedroom' is really a chamber, as in chamber pot.
annotation.definitionFit: Potty means daft; a potty is a small child's toilet pot.

entries.clue: Car manufacturer losing sales ultimately in first month (5)

indicators.note: the car maker loses something, so a letter drops out of its name
the letter removed is the last one of 'sales'

annotation.surface: A carmaker has a slump in sales at the start of the year.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First month' looks like January; it is the first month of the Jewish religious calendar.
annotation.definitionFit: Nisan is the first month of the Jewish ecclesiastical year.

entries.clue: Have chap insert pipe wrongly — what you get with learning on the job? (14)

definitions.text: what you get with learning on the job?

indicators.note: done incorrectly, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A trainee plumber fits a pipe badly, as you would expect while still learning.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a plumbing trainee's mistake, which is exactly what an apprenticeship allows for.
annotation.definitionFit: An apprenticeship is a period of training learned on the job.

entries.clue: Hesitant approach of amateur painter, maybe covering that place inadequately (7)

indicators.note: the approach wraps round the shortened word
not completely, so the last letter is cut

blocks.note: DIY = do-it-yourself, how an amateur decorator works
THERE = that place, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A novice painter works tentatively, only partly covering the surface.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Painter' suggests an artist, but it is someone painting their own walls.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone dithery keeps wavering and cannot make up their mind.

entries.clue: Famous biochemist first to sequence nettle (6)

indicators.note: take the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: to nettle is to irritate, anger

annotation.surface: A celebrated scientist was the first to sequence the nettle's genes.
annotation.walkthrough: Frederick Sanger really was a pioneer of sequencing proteins and DNA, so the surface fits him.
annotation.definitionFit: Frederick Sanger won two Nobel prizes in chemistry for sequencing work.
